proofs.text: Run the script with no action, with `--quick` and no feature, with `--quick --record`, with `--all --feature x`, with `--all --quick --commit`, with `--tier wide`, with `--nonsense` and with `--feature` and no value; verify each exits 2 and prints `Usage: purlin_run.py`

reasons: PROOF-1 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: The command line names exactly one of `--quick`, `--record` and `--remote`, and either `--all` or at least one `--feature`; `--commit`, `--ci` and `--tag` belong to `--record`; `--tier` is `unit` or `all`. Any other shape exits 2 and prints the usage line

def test_bad_invocation_exits_two(self, tmp_path, args):
        root = _project(tmp_path)
        code, output = _run(root, *args)
        assert code == 2, output
        assert 'Usage: purlin_run.py' in output
